51333294.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to LXRalpha (unknown origin) by surface plasmon resonance assay
references_previous: Reference 29: Wang, J. J.; Chen, F. M.; Liu, Y. H.; Liu, Y. X.; Li, K. L.; Yang, X. L.; Liu, S. W.; Zhou, X. F.; Yang, J. J. Nat. Prod. 2018, 81, 2722–2730.
Reference 30: Rossi, G.; Real-Fernández, F.; Panza, F.; Barbetti, F.; Pratesi, F.; Rovero, P.; Migliorini, P. Anal. Biochem. 2014, 465, 96–101.
Reference 18: Xu, P.; Li, D. B.; Tang, X. T.; Bao, X. H.; Huang, J.; Tang, Y. P.; Yang, Y.; Xu, H. W.; Fan, X. T. Mol. Neurobiol. 2013, 48, 715–728.

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - Surface Plasmon: In vitro SPR assay was conducted as previously reported.29 The binding affinities of 1 and 8 with the LXRα receptor were conducted using a Biacore T100 system from GE Healthcare.30 Briefly, 0.5 μM LXRα receptor protein was immobilized on a CM5 sensor chip (GE Healthcare) using a pH 5.0 acetic acid solution (Carlo Erba). Compounds 1 and 8 at different concentrations were injected for 180 s at a flow rate of 50 μL/min. A cleaning solution (50 mM NaOH) was used to regenerate the chip. The data were collected at 25 °C. KD values were calculated using Biacore Evaluation Software 2.0. The potent LXR agonist GW3965 was utilized as the positive control.18
original_paragraph.Figure 3B caption: The affinity of 8 to the LXRα receptor analyzed by SPR assay.
original_paragraph.Figure 3B sensorgram data: The sensorgram shows response (RU) over time (s). Concentrations of compound 8 are labeled on the curves: Cycle 1.5625 μM, Cycle 3.125 μM, Cycle 6.25 μM, Cycle 12.5 μM, Cycle 25 μM, Cycle 50 μM, Cycle 6.25 μM. The x-axis ranges from -10 to 250 s. The y-axis ranges from -5 to 40 RU. The KD value is explicitly stated as 50.0 μM.
original_paragraph.Results section - SPR assay: An in vitro surface plasmon resonance (SPR) assay was used to measure the affinity of the ligands with the LXRα receptor. Compound 8, with the highest S value (−11) of the receptor–ligand interactions in the docking study, combined well with the LXRα receptor in a dose-dependent manner. The kinetic curves of 8 (Figure 3B) are similar to those of the potent LXR agonist GW3965 (Figure S2) for binding with LXRα in the SPR assay, with the dissociation equilibrium constant (KD) of 50.0 μM (KD 20.6 μM for GW3965). In contrast, there is nearly no binding effect of 1 (lower S value −6.1 in docking) with LXRα in the SPR assay (Figure S2). Together with the docking analysis, it is suggested that the sugar group in 8 is beneficial for binding to LXRα.
